# Notebooks still carrying the blanket `warnings.filterwarnings("ignore")`.
#
# The standard used to prescribe it. `rules/notebook-standards.md` clause M2 was narrowed on
# 2026-09-08 (ml4t/agent-workspace#1096): suppress the noisy messages by name, filtered by
# category and module, and leave visible anything that may report a real problem -
# ConvergenceWarning and other optimization failures, RuntimeWarning for overflow,
# divide-by-zero and invalid value, and anything the notebook's own result depends on.
#
# These files predate that ruling and conform to the old one. They are listed rather than
# fixed because removing the call is a code-cell change: the provenance gate marks the
# notebook STALE and it has to be re-executed before it can be committed, which is correct -
# the point of the change is that renders start showing warnings, so the render has to be
# regenerated. 204 of the 243 files carrying the call are stamped, so this is a re-execution
# programme rather than a text sweep, and it proceeds a notebook at a time.
#
# HOW TO USE THIS FILE: when you re-execute a notebook for any reason, drop its blanket call
# first, name whatever noise the run then shows, and delete its line here. The list may only
# ever shrink - tests/test_blanket_warning_filters.py fails on an entry whose file no longer
# carries the call, so a stale line cannot sit here unnoticed, and it fails on a file that
# carries the call and is not listed, so a new notebook cannot add one.
#
# The four stage-04 notebooks in ml4t/agent-workspace#1095 are the sharpest case: they fork a
# worker pool from a process holding a BLAS thread pool and filter the 3.14 warning that says
# the child may deadlock. Two of the four are already fixed on this branch; cme_futures and
# fx_pairs are stamped and wait for a re-execution, and theirs must not regenerate
# features/model_based.parquet, whose sha256 keys every model fitted against it.
